subject: Post-call: Jupiter Health performance targets and customer-run test onboarding
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Jupiter Health performance targets and customer-run test onboarding

Hi Emma — thanks again for the productive call just now. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before your customer-led run: 

Summary of targets you confirmed on the call:
- Latency: p95 inference latency target <= 250 ms (payloads average ~1k tokens)
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/sec for 30 minutes, ramp to 500 rps for a 5-minute spike test
- Concurrency: up to 80 concurrent streaming sessions (we'll treat these as long-lived SSE connections)
- Streaming behavior: chunked responses, keep-alive KV cache warmup required for accurate tail latency

What Redwood will provide before the test:
1) A dedicated test endpoint and a short-lived service account for sandbox calls (scoped, revocable).
2) A k6-compatible scenario that mirrors the call pattern we discussed (attached as jupiter_k6_scenario_v1.js).
3) A one-page runbook with checklist and emergency rollback steps (attached).
4) On-call SE presence during your window + a small temporary throughput uplift so our SLO rules do not prematurely throttle during the run.

What we need from your side to finalize scheduling:
- Final test window (start/end in UTC) — you mentioned late May 21–22 UTC; please confirm the exact 2-hour window.
- List of public IPs or ranges your load generators will use so we can update the allowlist.
- Confirmation you want streaming sessions exercised (yes/no) and which scenario to prioritize (cold-cache vs warm-cache).
- Point of contact and Slack/phone number for the run day for rapid coordination.

Attachments: jupiter_k6_scenario_v1.js (k6 script), jupiter_customer_runbook_v1.pdf, service_account_instructions.txt

If that all looks right I can spin up the test endpoint and post credentials by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emma Li <emma.li@jupiterhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Load Team <load-testing@jupiterhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@jupiterhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Jupiter Health performance targets and customer-run test onboarding

Thanks Jonas — that recap is spot on. A few clarifications from our side before you provision anything: 

1) Test window: tentative preferred window is 2027-05-22 02:00–04:00 UTC (we run off-hours to avoid covariate traffic spikes). Can you confirm Redwood can be on-call then?
2) Load generator IPs: our initial run will come from the following ranges (we'll lock these down by EOD Friday): 52.24.134.0/24 (primary) and 34.88.190.12/32 (fallback). Is that format OK for your allowlist?
3) Streaming: yes, please exercise streaming. We want a 70/30 split warm-cache/cold-cache. Warm-cache scenario should pre-warm with 100 short prompts for 15 minutes prior to the sustained window.
4) Service account: we prefer a bearer token and a one-minute TTL demo token pattern if possible. Otherwise provide instructions for scoped keys.

Point of contact for the run: Raj Patel (raj.patel@jupiterhealth.com), Slack: #jupiter-load.

Emma
Emma Li
Product Ops — Jupiter Health
emma.li@jupiterhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@jupiterhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Jupiter Health performance targets and customer-run test onboarding

Hi Emma — Ben (SE) here. I pulled the runbook and scripts into our test folder and prepared the service-account instructions. Quick notes: 

- Allowlist format: the two CIDRs you listed are fine. We'll also add a small set of Redwood egress IPs for callbacks: 18.205.93.0/24 and 3.210.45.12/32. Please confirm with your security team if they prefer hostnames instead.
- Token: we can issue a short-lived bearer token that you can rotate from the Console. For the test I'll provision a token valid for the 24-hour window around the run and tag it so it auto-revokes.
- Endpoint: https://sandbox.jupiter.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate (note: sandbox is isolated and will mirror the prod model variant we discussed).

Attached: jupiter_k6_scenario_v1.js (the script includes separate scenarios: warm_cache, cold_cache, and spike), jupiter_customer_runbook_v1.pdf (on-call checklist), service_account_instructions.txt (how to exchange the test token).

Two quick asks for your load team before we finalize: 
1) Confirm exact IP list before 12:00 (PST) on 2027-05-21 so we have time to propagate allowlists.
2) Confirm whether the spike test should be an instantaneous jump to 500 rps or a 3-minute ramp; our recommendation is a 3-minute ramp to avoid network-level SYN bursts.

I will provision the test token and post the link to the Drive folder once you confirm the IPs and spike behavior.

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@jupiterhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Jupiter Health performance targets and customer-run test onboarding

Thanks Ben — confirmed items from ops: 

- Final load generator IPs for the May 22 window (will be the sources seen by Redwood): 52.24.134.12/32, 52.24.134.13/32, 34.88.190.12/32. Please add these three to the allowlist.
- Test window confirmed: 2027-05-22 02:00–04:00 UTC. We'll run: 15-minute warmup (pre-warm 100 prompts), 30-minute sustained at target 300 rps, 5-minute 3-minute ramp-to-500 spike, then 10-minute cool-down.
- We'll exercise streaming concurrently at ~60 active streams during the sustained window.
- We will use the k6 script you provided with a single modification (adjusted think-time to 250 ms).

On-call phone for the run: +1 (617) 555-0199 (Raj). We'll join your on-call Slack channel and provide run-time telemetry to your SE.

Please post the sandbox token and the final allowlist confirmations.

Raj
Raj Patel
Ops Lead — Jupiter Health
raj.patel@jupiterhealth.com

All good — thank you for locking the window and IPs. Final confirmations from Redwood side below and a short checklist for Monday's run: 

Redwood confirmations:
- Allowlist applied: 52.24.134.12/32, 52.24.134.13/32, 34.88.190.12/32 added to the sandbox firewall rules; callbacks permitted from 18.205.93.0/24 and 3.210.45.12/32.
- Sandbox token: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JUP-TestToken (temporary bearer token instructions in service_account_instructions.txt). Token valid from 2027-05-21 12:00 UTC to 2027-05-23 12:00 UTC.
- On-call support: Ben will be on Slack and on-call phone during the entire window. Marissa will monitor SLO dashboards and logs.
- Temporary throughput uplift: we will remove automated per-key throttles for the sandbox endpoint during the run window to avoid early throttling; standard platform protections (rate limiting at the tenant boundary) will be relaxed for your test tag only.

Run-day checklist (please confirm by 2027-05-21 12:00 PST):
- Confirm the final k6 script (we have your think-time change noted).
- Confirm your run start time in UTC (we have 02:00).
- Confirm Slack channel membership for Raj and one backup contact.
